I'm a 44-year-old woman who's farmed this land in Quzhou for 20 years. My husband works construction in Handan and sends money home, and my son is in high school in the county town, so day-to-day it's mostly me and my mother-in-law managing the 13.1 mu. I finished middle school, so I can read the extension leaflets, but honestly I trust what I've seen with my own eyes more than what some young technician tells me.

It's mid-October now. I just got the summer maize off the 8 mu wheat-maize fields — got about 480 kg/mu, which is decent. The cotton on the other 5.1 mu is almost done picking too. I need to get the winter wheat in the ground within the next week or the cold will hurt the stand.

For the wheat, I'm planting the same improved variety I've used for three years. The seed dealer always pushes new hybrids, but this one works and I know it. I'll drill about 10 kg/mu. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer as base — about 40 kg/mu of the 15-15-15 type. Then in April at jointing I'll topdress with urea, about 20 kg/mu. The extension station says 15 kg N per mu is the "scientific" rate, but two years ago I tried cutting back to that and my yield dropped to 380 kg/mu. Never again. I do about 16 kg N total. I'll irrigate three times: wintering water in November or December, jointing water in April, and one more at grain filling in May. The well is metered now and each irrigation costs nearly 30 yuan per mu, so that's almost 900 yuan just for wheat water, but you can't skip jointing water — I've seen what drought at that stage does. For pesticides, I spray herbicide once in spring when the weeds are small. Wheat harvest I'll hire the combine — costs about 50 yuan/mu but saves my back.

For cotton, I finished the last picking yesterday. Got about 230 kg/mu of seed cotton. The buyer is paying 7.5 yuan/kg this year, so I'm keeping the 5.1 mu in cotton for next year rather than switching it to grain. I'll plant hybrid seed in mid-to-late April — you can't save cotton seed, it doesn't grow true. Cotton needs more management than grain. Base fertilizer is compound, then I topdress twice: once at flowering and once at boll-setting. Total about 14 kg N/mu. I'll irrigate twice, at flowering and boll-setting. The real cost is pesticide and labor — bollworm is always a threat, so I spray 4 or 5 times. Picking is the killer. My daughter will help during the October holiday, but for the main picking I'll hire women from the village. That's 150 yuan per mu for picking alone.

For maize, I won't plant until mid-June next year, right after wheat harvest. The window is brutally tight — sometimes only 5 or 6 days between wheat coming off and maize needing to be in the ground. I'll hire a tractor to do shallow tillage, then plant immediately. Hybrid seed, about 2 kg/mu. Base fertilizer of compound at planting, then urea at the big trumpet stage — about 15 kg N total. One or two irrigations depending on the summer rains. Last year was dry so I did two; if it's a normal year, once at silking is enough. I spray herbicide once and maybe insecticide if I see corn borer.

I have about 7,000 yuan saved for inputs this season. Wheat will take about 2,500, maize about 2,400, and cotton about 3,000. That adds to roughly 6,800 yuan, which leaves me a small cushion. My husband's off-farm income means we're not desperate, but I still watch every yuan — there's always a doctor's bill or school fee around the corner. I expect about 450 kg/mu from wheat, 500 kg/mu from maize, and if the weather cooperates, 240 kg/mu of seed cotton.
